claim.pdf_says:
15.13.2   General format

  FUNCTION  BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER  ( argument-1  argument-2 )      [FUNCTION and BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER are both UNDERLINED in the printed general format]
claim.why_it_matters: Underlining in a general format is normative notation (5.2.6): an underlined word is a REQUIRED word. The transcription drops the underline on both FUNCTION and BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER and renders the format as inline code. specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 34265, against the `<u>…</u>` convention used for the same construct at COMBINED-DATETIME (line 34452) and CONCAT (line 34500) a few clauses later.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED after independent inspection of both sources; the claim survives every refutation attempt I could mount.

1. PRINTED GLYPHS (E:/Temp/specrecon/v852/spec_p852.png, 300 dpi, printed folio 822 = PDF page 852; cropped and upscaled to E:/Temp/specrecon/v852/crop_fmt.png). Under 15.13.2 the page prints a single format line: FUNCTION  BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER  ( argument-1  argument-2 ). I looked at the strokes directly. There are TWO distinct horizontal rules beneath the line: one spanning exactly the extent of FUNCTION (starting at the F, ending after the N, with a clear gap before the next word) and a second spanning exactly BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER (starting at the B, ending after the final R). Both rules stop well short of the opening parenthesis; the parenthesized argument group '( argument-1  argument-2 )' carries NO rule. These are word-scoped underlines, not a table rule, a page rule, or a scan artifact — a stray rule would not break at the inter-word space nor terminate precisely at a word boundary. So the printed standard underlines both words and only those two words.

2. MARKDOWN (specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 34265, verified by direct read, and reproduced identically in the work-unit slice E:/Temp/specrecon/v852/page-852.md line 19): the line is `FUNCTION BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER ( argument-1 argument-2 )` — a backtick inline-code span with no underline markup of any kind. The claim quotes BOTH sources verbatim and correctly.

3. NOT REFLOW, NOT FURNITURE, NOT WRAPPING. Every word, the punctuation, and the operand order match the PDF exactly; the only deltas are inter-word spacing (immaterial). Nothing is 'missing on an adjacent line' — the lost item is not text but NOTATION. This cannot be dismissed as cosmetic formatting because in this document the underline IS the normative discriminator: 5.2.2 Keywords (line 2631) — 'They are shown in uppercase and underlined in general formats. They are required…'; 5.2.3 Optional words (line 2646) — 'uppercase words that are not underlined are called optional words'; restated at 8.3.2.4.2 (line 5773) and 8.3.2.4.3 (line 5808). Applying the standard's own rule to line 34265 as transcribed yields the FALSE conclusion that FUNCTION and BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER are optional words.

4. THE FILE'S OWN CONVENTION CONFIRMS THE LOSS. specs/ISO_COBOL.md encodes printed underlines as `<u>…</u>`. Twenty sibling intrinsic-function general formats do exactly that — `<u>FUNCTION</u> <u>ABS</u> …` (34026), `<u>FUNCTION</u> <u>COMBINED-DATETIME</u> …` (34452), `<u>FUNCTION</u> <u>CONCAT</u> …` (34500) — and at 38573 the convention is load-bearing inside a single format: `<u>FUNCTION</u> <u>UPPER-CASE</u> ( argument-1 [ <u>LOCALE</u> locale-name-1 ] )`, where the underline marks LOCALE required within an optional bracket. So the markup exists, is used for this exact construct, and was simply not applied at 34265.

5. ADVERSARIAL DISCOUNT, STATED HONESTLY. For THIS particular format the practical parsing impact is nil: the format contains no optional uppercase words, and FUNCTION plus the function-name are unconditionally required in every intrinsic-function reference, so no implementer would actually mis-derive syntax from line 34265. That is why this is a notation-fidelity defect rather than a semantics defect. It remains real because the transcription contradicts the printed page and its own stated convention.

Verdict: real content discrepancy, correctly identified and correctly quoted, with two inaccuracies in the claim's framing (see corrected_description).
verdict.corrected_description:
REAL, with two corrections to the claim's framing.

(a) WRONG CITATION. The claim cites 5.2.6 for 'underlined word = REQUIRED word'. 5.2.6 is 'Options' and governs brackets, braces and choice indicators only (5.2.6.1–5.2.6.4, specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 2683–2704) — it says nothing about underlining. The governing clauses are 5.2.2 Keywords ('shown in uppercase and underlined in general formats… They are required', line 2631) and 5.2.3 Optional words ('uppercase words that are not underlined', line 2646), restated normatively at 8.3.2.4.2 Required words (line 5773) and 8.3.2.4.3 Optional words (line 5808). Any ledger entry should cite 5.2.2/5.2.3 (+8.3.2.4.2/8.3.2.4.3), not 5.2.6.

(b) UNDERSTATED SCOPE — this is a systemic pattern, not a one-line slip, so the fix is a sweep and not a single edit. In Chapter 15, 21 intrinsic-function general formats are rendered as plain backtick inline code with the underline dropped from BOTH words: lines 34152 (ASIN), 34265 (BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER), 34412 (CHAR-NATIONAL), 34699 (COS), 34786 (DATE-OF-INTEGER), 35005 (DISPLAY-OF), 35047 (E), 35148 (EXCEPTION-FILE-N), 35954 (INTEGER-OF-DATE), 35994 (INTEGER-OF-DAY), 36255 (LOCALE-DATE), 36386 (LOG), 36421 (LOG10), 36670 (MEDIAN), 36761 (MIN), 36912 (NATIONAL-OF), 37148 (NUMVAL-F), 37219 (ORD), 37749 (SIN), 38115 (TAN), 38723 (YEAR-TO-YYYY). Two further formats are half-transcribed — the underline is present on FUNCTION but lost on the function-name: line 34556 `<u>FUNCTION</u> CONVERT (…)` and line 38296 `<u>FUNCTION</u> TEST-NUMVAL (…)`. Only 20 formats carry the full `<u>FUNCTION</u> <u>NAME</u>` markup. Correct remedy: rewrite all 23 defective lines to `<u>FUNCTION</u> <u>NAME</u> ( … )`, matching the 20 correct siblings, after confirming each against its own printed page.

(c) SEVERITY NOTE. 'structural' is defensible as a notation-fidelity defect but overstates the operational risk for this specific format: the format has no optional uppercase words, and FUNCTION and the function-name are required in every intrinsic-function reference regardless, so no wrong syntax can be derived from the degraded line in practice. Rate it as a notation/convention-fidelity defect to be fixed as a batch sweep, not as a semantics-changing error.
